findings.reason: the node would implement a wait the plan names but its own answering mechanism cannot resolve, so the DAG claim §8 exists to make fails exactly for plan-level dependencies.
findings.text: §8 defines a request's waits as the union of its section's refs, its plan's `depends_on`, its section's gates and `--after` refs, then answers every wait through "one per-section predicate ... reading every hold field the roadmap row carries", listing `section_readiness`, `section_gate_blockers`, `gate_blockers`, `explicit_blockers` and `held_blockers`; but a plan-level `depends_on` is not among them — `build_roadmap` computes `plan_dependency_blockers` only to set the plan-level `readiness`/`effective_status` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3359-3362`, `:3438-3448`) and attaches it to no row field, while `section_readiness` is built solely from `section_dependency_blockers` and `decision_section_blockers` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3583-3600`); `after_hold` is the soft `after` edge, not `depends_on` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3426`). s8 also forbids the one place the fact exists ("A wait is answered per section, never from the plan-level summary"), and the cycle graph's nodes are fixed as "sections and requests", so a plan-level ref has no node to land on and a mutual plan-level dependency is not detectable there. As written, a request whose plan declares an unmet `depends_on` launches anyway, and the union's fourth component is unanswerable

findings.reason: the section reintroduces the silent-unreadable-status stall its own evidence names, and one added obligation line (or a move to `blocked-upstream`) is all the mechanism needs.
findings.text: §8 says `completed`, `done`, `landed` and `promoted` are refused by `parse_manifest` and that "a waiter whose upstream manifest uses one of them stays held until the status is repaired", while the plan raises an owning-session obligation for its sibling case (a row with no `promoted_revision`) and §2 raises one for `blocked-upstream`; the unreadable-manifest hold raises nothing — `_request_state` catches `ManifestParseError` and returns `PENDING` with no obligation (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1230-1240`), so the request waits silently and the coordinator is never woken. §1's own measured evidence is precisely this failure ("One unreadable status held the chain for two hours" until a `crew repair --status complete` released it), and §6's wake list covers only `blocked`/`failed` runs and `blocked-upstream` requests, so no pass ever surfaces it. An upstream run that genuinely delivered but carries one of these words holds its whole downstream chain with no signal

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every named anchor resolves in the tree: `_readiness_rows` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1056`), `_readiness_by_slug` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:3094`, which does keep one verdict per plan), `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES` at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1023` with exactly `("complete", "completed", "done", "landed", "promoted")`, `MANIFEST_STATUSES`/`TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES` in `reckon/crew/reports.py:126-140` (whose union confirms `completed`, `done`, `landed` and `promoted` are outside it and so refused by `parse_manifest`), the promotion-time `ledger.append_run` (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:1631`), `run_path` (`reckon/ledger.py:890`), `sweep_promoted_revisions` with `target_head="HEAD"` and the project-mount checkout (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:1985-2030`), `parse_plan_ref` (`reckon/_schema.py:276`), `TaskNode` (`reckon/crew/node.py:725`) and `reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §8 states a measurable battery with a declared negative arm ("The negative arm declares B's §2 done before queuing, and the request goes straight to `queued`") and refusal arms that assert nothing is stored; the two mechanisms that have no arm are raised under `reasoning` rather than as a done-when defect.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §8's owners name `a new test file` among durable write paths in `reckon/crew/`, and no gate log or artifact is placed on a scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §8 introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into code, and its prose states mechanisms rather than changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding, twice — §8 puts `its plan's depends_on` into a request's wait union but the only answering path it defines (a per-section predicate over hold fields the roadmap row carries) cannot see a plan-level dependency, and §8 accepts a silent permanent hold for an unreadable upstream manifest, which is the failure §1 was written to remove.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 carries one deliverable, a queue whose waits are answered by the work's DAG across plans and projects; the readiness-assembly factoring, the `complete` narrowing and the landed check are all in service of that one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §8's declared edge (`s8` → `a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan#s2`) matches what the section consumes (`_readiness_rows`, `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES` and the awaiting-upstream phases all come from §2), and no relationship it needs is missing or points elsewhere.
